build.builders_own_ruling: KEEP the mechanism, do not claim F7. The build declined its own acceptance, reported that two of five poses regress, that the water is 8-14% darker at every pose, and that its only positive result is contradicted by its own second instrument. It named the counter-position explicitly (set the default to 1e-4).

bifurcation.fidelity: Judged against modern references only: `RI-VIS04` §9's MIN BAR and TELL, `RI-WLD10` §10's fidelity clause, `RI-VIS03` M12/M12a. Every pixel number below is on this side.
bifurcation.art_direction: `RI-WLD10` §10.1 — 'water is opaque before it is reflective' — is cited on the art-direction side, judged against Morrowind/`RI-WLD05` conventions and against the province's own declared `k` table, not against a modern plate. It is the clause the shipped alpha term contradicts.

the_headline: The mechanism the r3 verdict asked for is genuinely built — `esBandM` contains no `k`, which three lines of shader settle without measurement. But at the shipped 1.20 m the term is non-zero over 65.1% of the Deep Marshes water in frame and 98.6% of the Western Rootlands water in frame, so it is a transparency multiplier over the water body rather than a shoreline fade — ONE cause for both of the symptoms the build reported as two. And it is tunable, against the build's own conclusion: swept at the pose carrying its only positive result, `gradient_width_px` is FLAT AT 34 px from 0.10 m to 1.20 m while `presence` falls monotonically from 50.6% to 40.7%. The shipped constant is dominated by one twelve times smaller.

job_1_the_census.asked: Verify the census independently. If it holds, three rounds of F7 reasoning rest on a mis-sited camera.
job_1_the_census.ruling: CONFIRMED to the digit, in my own code, without importing the build's tool. vista-deep-marshes within 120 m: 121 water cells, 47 waterline (38.84%), nearest 17.7 m, q-saturation 0.2416. The two seas: Marauder's Coast 0.9248 / 4 waterline / nearest 81.0 m; Crimson Coast 0.9706 / 4 / 60.5 m. The Deep Marshes is not shoreless; what was true is a POSE fact about round 3's 4.5-7 m close-ups.
job_1_the_census.and_it_is_wrong_in_the_CORPUS_not_only_i: `RI-VIS03` §M12a clause 4 states as a worked example that 'the Deep Marshes is WCI 0.86; three rounds of F7 shot every frame there and not one frame contains a shoreline.' Every future critic inherits it. Amended in place under CRITIC-DOCTRINE §1.3 — rule untouched, no threshold relaxed, only the false example corrected, exactly as ARBITRATION S60, S63 and S65 each had to correct their own narrations.

job_2_the_acceptance_and_the_ruling_the_.the_acceptance_fails: Confirmed. The r3 remedy's clause is `gradient_width_px >= 12` at a declared `water_edge` pose in the Deep Marshes over a pinned mask; M12a clause 3 makes a band met only at the worst pose. Worst pose is 1 px. It fails at every threshold and in both regions.

the_water_presence_control_which_nobody_.what: Every artifact dir carries a `--water-hidden` frame (all 93 water meshes hidden) and no round has scored it. presence = (L[arm] - L[hidden]) / (L[prefix] - L[hidden]) over the pinned mask.
the_water_presence_control_which_nobody_.threshold_independence: 41.1 / 41.2 / 41.4 at thresholds 4 / 6 / 10 — unlike `gradient_width_px`, this measure does not depend on the threshold.
the_water_presence_control_which_nobody_.the_decomposition_the_round_had_the_arms: At edge-b135 the depth COLOUR alone (`no-shorefade`) leaves 89.4%. Round 3's k-gated alpha takes it to 59.5%; round 4's band to 41.2%. Of 58.8 points lost, 10.6 are colour and 48.2 are the shoreline ALPHA term. The build's defence that 'the colour half is deliberately untouched' does not reach the cost.

why_the_band_is_not_a_shoreline_band.method: esDepthM = clamp((q-0.43)/0.57,0,1)*1.35 is the exact inverse of province.js's q, so a wet corner's esDepthM IS its depth in metres and esBandM can be evaluated offline over the same WorldField.
why_the_band_is_not_a_shoreline_band.ruling: The constant sits ABOVE the median water depth in both regions. RI-VIS04 §9's MIN BAR component is a SHORELINE depth fade; a term acting on 98.6% of the water in frame is not one. This is also why the Western Rootlands width went 5 -> 1: a fade applied uniformly has no edge to measure.
why_the_band_is_not_a_shoreline_band.how_the_constant_was_chosen: water.js's own comment and the status justify 1.20 m because '71 of 121 water cells carry a corner shallower than 1.20 m, so it spans effectively the whole graded population'. Maximal coverage is the goal of a depth tint. A shoreline band wants MINIMAL coverage. The selection criterion is the inverse of the requirement.

the_sweep_the_round_never_ran.why_the_builds_sweep_could_not_settle_it: It covered 0.60 / 1.20 / 1.35 — all above the median wet-corner depth in frame, i.e. entirely inside the broad regime.
the_sweep_the_round_never_ran.ruling: THE WIDTH IS FLAT AT 34 px ACROSS A 12x RANGE OF THE CONSTANT AND ONLY THE DARKENING MOVES. 'No band constant rescues it, so it is not a tuning problem' is false as stated. What is true is narrower: the width is a STEP function of whether a band exists at all, not a function of its size — and beyond existence the constant buys nothing but absence.
the_sweep_the_round_never_ran.what_i_did_NOT_establish: I ran this at edge-b135 only. The build's failing pose is edge-b225, where I did not test below 0.60. Nobody should read 'a small band rescues edge-b225' into this table.

job_2_the_acceptance_and_the_ruling_the_.MY_RULING: KEEP the mechanism. REJECT the shipped default. Set `uWaterShoreBandM` to 0.10 m — not 1.20 and not 1e-4. The build framed the choice as keep-at-1.20 versus revert-to-1e-4; on the numbers both are wrong, because 1.20 is dominated on the build's own instrument by a constant that holds the entire width and returns ten points of presence. It is one number and exactly as reversible as the build's own.

blind_comparisons.would_it_have_changed_the_verdict: It could only have lowered RI-WLD10, never raised it — the item is already at 2 for measured reasons. But it is the ONE instrument that could settle the question neither the build nor I can: whether a 34 px luma ramp across a surface that reads as dark bed is worth 59 points of water presence to anybody. That is a look question and it is exactly what the unrun gate is for. On my evidence I would expect round 2 to win at edge-b135 against both later arms.

bar_findings.what: The clause asserts as a worked example: 'The Deep Marshes is WCI 0.86; three rounds of F7 shot every frame there and not one frame contains a shoreline.' Measured against the same WorldField the engine builds: 47 of 121 water cells within 120 m of the vista-deep-marshes stand are waterline cells, the nearest at 17.7 m, and 75.8% of wet corners carry a live depth gradient. The claim is false and it is in the BAR, where every future critic inherits it.
bar_findings.action: Amended in place under CRITIC-DOCTRINE §1.3. The rule — a water_edge pose with a real boundary, and a WCI rule for regions that have none — is untouched, and no threshold is relaxed. Only the false worked example is corrected, and the correct instrument (a field census before any capture) is named in its place. This is the same act ARBITRATION S60, S63 and S65 each had to perform on their own narrations.

score.band_label: min over the three items this piece can move: RI-WLD10 2, RI-VIS04 4, RI-VIS03 2. DOWN FROM 3. It falls because the delivered state of the game is worse where a player starts: the shipped arm leaves 41.2% of round 2's visible water at the worst pose, is 8-14% darker at every pose measured, and contradicts RI-WLD10 §10.1's opacity clause over 65-99% of the water in frame — a defect that applies to round 3 as well and that no round had measured. It is NOT lowered for the build's honesty, which is the best thing in the round: three of my findings only exist because it banked the arms that falsify it.
score.confidence: high on the census (re-derived in my own code, matches to the digit), on the presence control (threshold-independent across 4/6/10, and visible in the frames), on the band-distribution arithmetic (offline, deterministic) and on the sort test (arithmetic on banked numbers). High on the ordinal confound, because `no-shorefade` is a falsifier rather than a correlation. MEDIUM on the band sweep, because it is one pose in one process with no S52 null under it — the same weakness I am charging the build with, and I say so. LOW on anything about motion: I have stills from five bearings and no motion sequence.

the_builders_ruling.it_said: KEEP the mechanism, do not claim F7; a critic weighting 'the starting region's water reads as more absent' above 'the mechanism is now correct' should set the default to 1e-4.
the_builders_ruling.my_ruling: KEEP the mechanism. REJECT the shipped default. SET IT TO 0.10 m — neither of the two options offered. The build's pair is false because it assumes the constant is not the variable: swept, the width is flat at 34 px from 0.10 m to 1.20 m and only the darkening moves, so 1.20 m is dominated on the build's own instrument.
the_builders_ruling.and_it_was_right_about_the_bigger_thing: It declined its own acceptance, published the fourth bearing that turned its FresnelDelta row from an apparent pass into a fail, kept a void run on disk labelled void, wrote up the branch-wide defect it caused as a hazard for everyone else, and caught its own inherited census error by running the command rather than quoting the verdict. A round that had graded itself would have shipped '1 px -> 34 px'.

biggest_gap.what: `uWaterShoreBandM`'s default of 1.20 m exceeds the median water depth in both measured regions (Deep Marshes 0.824 m, Western Rootlands 0.375 m), so the term is non-zero over 65.1% and 98.6% of the water in frame respectively. It therefore acts as a depth-driven transparency multiplier over the water body rather than as a shoreline fade — which produces BOTH of the round's reported symptoms from one cause: a fade applied nearly everywhere has almost no edge (no gradient), and it lowers alpha nearly everywhere (the water reads as absent, worst-pose presence 41.2%).
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: RI-VIS04 §9's MIN BAR component is a SHORELINE depth fade and this is not one. RI-WLD10 §10.1 — 'water is opaque before it is reflective' — is contradicted by a term that drops diffuseColor.a to 0.42x over most of the surface. And the Deep Marshes is the starting region and the first water anybody sees, so the cost lands exactly where the owner would look first.

remedy.action: In game/src/render/water.js, F7's own file, in this order. (a) Set `uWaterShoreBandM`'s default to 0.10 m — measured to hold the full 34 px width at edge-b135 while returning ten points of presence over the shipped constant. (b) Re-sweep 0.10 / 0.20 / 0.30 at edge-b225 and in the Western Rootlands, because the failing pose was never tested below 0.60 m by anybody. (c) Report `presence` against the `water-hidden` frame on every row — the control already exists in every capture and has never been scored.
remedy.acceptance: gradient_width_px >= 12 at the WORST pose of a complete 4-bearing declared set in the Deep Marshes, measured at THRESHOLD 10 (the only threshold whose mask arm is stable here: drift +0.01 / -1.66 / -0.52 / +0.20% against +61.75 / +51.07 / +33.56 / -0.03% at threshold 6); AND presence >= 90% at every pose in BOTH regions against the water-hidden frame taken in the same process (the shipped arm reads 41.2% at its worst pose); AND the band leaves >= 60% of wet corners untouched in BOTH regions, measured offline against the WorldField (the shipped 1.20 m leaves 34.9% in the Deep Marshes and 1.4% in the Western Rootlands); AND the arms run in BOTH orders at one pose so own_mask_delta_pct can be attributed to the arm rather than to capture ordinal. Per S64, a pose whose declared target has every wet corner beyond the band (edge-b045's are 1.433-1.492 m) scores `inapplicable` and must name the absence, never pass.

acceptance_clause_provenance.improving: gradient_width_px >= 12 at the WORST pose of a complete 4-bearing declared set in the Deep Marshes, measured at THRESHOLD 10 — the only threshold whose mask arm is stable on this scene (measured drift +0.01 / -1.66 / -0.52 / +0.20% against +61.75 / +51.07 / +33.56 / -0.03% at threshold 6).
acceptance_clause_provenance.preserving_1: presence >= 90% at every pose in both regions, against the `water-hidden` frame taken in the same process. This is what stops the width being bought by deleting the water, which is the mechanism S59 exists to catch and which round 4 hit at 41.2%.
acceptance_clause_provenance.preserving_2: the band's coverage, measured offline against the WorldField, leaves >= 60% of wet corners untouched in BOTH regions — the clause that keeps a shoreline term shore-local.
acceptance_clause_provenance.attribution: the arms run in BOTH orders at one pose, so `own_mask_delta_pct` can be attributed to the arm rather than to the capture ordinal. Without it that number is not evidence of anything.

what_would_make_this_verdict_wrong: If `presence` is the wrong measure. It is a ratio of masked mean luma differences against a water-hidden frame, so it assumes the water's contribution is monotone in luma. In a marsh whose bed is darker than the water that holds, and the arms bracket it (prefix 100%, hidden 0%). But an arm that made water DARKER for a good reason would score low on it, and I have not built a control that distinguishes 'correctly darker' from 'absent'. THAT CONTROL IS THE BLIND PAIR, and it has not run.

If the band sweep's flatness is an artefact of one pose. It is one pose in one process. Three of the four Deep Marshes bearings behave differently from edge-b135 on every measure in this round, and I did not sweep any of them.

If my ordinal reading is wrong because `no-shorefade` is not the arm I think it is. It sets uWaterShoreFade = 0, which zeroes the alpha term; if the round-4 code path changes alpha by some other route the falsifier fails. I read the three shader lines and it does not.
If threshold 10 is stable only by luck at these five poses. Four poses is a small sample for an instrument claim, and I did not replicate it.

If lowering the score from 3 to 2 double-counts a defect that was present at round 3. The §10.1 opacity finding DOES apply to round 3 (presence 59.5%) and no round had measured it. I score the state of the game, and the state is worse than round 3's; but a reader who thinks the score should track the round's own delta rather than the state would leave it at 3, and that reading is defensible.

notes: The most useful thing in this round for anybody who is not working on water: `own_mask_delta_pct` looked like a clean 20x effect and is a capture-order artefact, and it was only detectable because the build banked an arm (`no-shorefade`) whose alpha is identical to the pin's. An instrument's own null arm, captured LAST, is the cheapest ordinal control there is — and no measurement sequence in this project currently runs one.
